clue.text: Meaningful nudge from flamboyant bird with hat on

indicators.note: flamboyant suggests a showy, wild display, so the letters of these words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A showy bird wearing a hat gives someone a pointed nudge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flamboyant' shuffles BIRD, HAT and ON together; 'from' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed suggestion that leaves little doubt is a meaningful nudge, the idiom for an obvious clue.

clue.text: Rough hop over grassland

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance, as is a ball
a park is an expanse of grass

explanation.surface: A rough skip across a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' is the adjective approximate, as in a ballpark figure, not a description of the hop.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpark figure is an approximate estimate, so the word serves as an adjective meaning rough.

clue.text: Brutes turn up on brief vacation

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to go is to take a turn, as in a game

indicators.note: brief means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a vacation is a rest from work

explanation.surface: Thugs show up while someone is away on a short holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses GO to OG; 'brief' trims REST to RES, and 'on' places OG above RES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are monstrous, cruel giants of folklore, so brutes in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Could it make duos celebrate end of alliance?

definitions.text: Could it make duos celebrate end of alliance?

indicators.note: the question asks what these letters could be made into, so the words duos and celebrate are rearranged
end of picks out the final letter of the word alliance

explanation.surface: Might something give a couple reason to party when their union finishes?
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of DUOS CELEBRATE plus E, the last letter of 'alliance', gives the answer, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree absolute is the final court order dissolving a marriage, which some divorced couples might celebrate.

clue.text: Provincial half of army behind endless abuse

indicators.note: behind places the second piece after the first
endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: abuse in words is insult

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the four letters of army

explanation.surface: Half a regiment trailing after relentless verbal attack, in a parochial mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts INSULT to INSUL; 'half of' takes AR from 'army', which goes 'behind' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Insular and provincial both describe narrow-minded people whose outlook ignores the wider world.

clue.text: Mention not getting a rise, masking pained expression

indicators.note: masking means the outer letters cover and hide the inner piece
in a down entry, a rise means the word is read upwards, so not is reversed

parts.note: ouch is what someone says when hurt

explanation.surface: Bring a subject up without provoking anyone, while hiding a wince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rise' suggests provoking someone, but in a down entry 'getting a rise' turns the word upwards to TON, which is 'masking' the wince.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch on a topic is to refer to it briefly, which is to mention it.

clue.text: Party organiser needing wife's help in public at first

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A political organiser who needs a spouse to help out in public.
explanation.walkthrough: A whip is the parliamentary official who keeps a party's members voting in line; 'Party' sounds like a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: In Parliament a whip organises a party's members and ensures they turn out for votes.

clue.text: US author may finally retire

parts.note: may is another name for the hawthorn bush and its blossom

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word retire

explanation.surface: An American writer who might eventually stop working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may' looks like a verb but is the blossom of the hawthorn tree. Nathaniel Hawthorne wrote The Scarlet Letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathaniel Hawthorne was a nineteenth-century American novelist, so an example of a US author.

clue.text: Where Pedro gets drinks bill when work's over?

indicators.note: over means the whole string is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a bill is a poster or advert, an ad
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A Spaniard settles up for his drinks once the working day ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses AD, AS and OP. A posada is a Spanish inn; Pedro marks it as Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: A posada is an inn or tavern in Spain, the sort of place a Spaniard named Pedro would drink.

clue.text: Bluecoat scores badly in showjumping event, say

indicators.note: badly means the letters of the two words are put together wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A rider in blue scores poorly in a showjumping competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A showjumping round is a course of fences to clear, an example of an obstacle course.

clue.text: Particularly rich passage from 26?

definitions.note: 26 is the poet, and this is something that comes from one

indicators.note: a passage is a stretch of text, here letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: An especially rich extract from a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 across is POET; a lyric is a short poem, the kind of thing a poet produces.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric is a short poem expressing feeling, the typical work of a poet.

clue.text: Dishes made from very high game

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
up means high, as in up in the air
bowls is a lawn game played with weighted balls

explanation.surface: Dishes made from meat that has hung far too long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high game' suggests well-hung meat, but splits into very, high and game.
explanation.definitionFit: Soup bowls are a kind of tableware, so they are dishes.

clue.text: Old-fashioned, essentially dull dance

parts.note: passé means out of date

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the central letters of the word dull

explanation.surface: A dated, rather boring dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pas seul is a solo dance in ballet.

clue.text: Henry longed to get married

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
to itch for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Henry yearned to marry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry' looks like a groom but gives only H, the physics unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting hitched is informal for getting married, so hitched means wed.

clue.text: Long-distance supplier of Meals on Wheels?

definitions.text: Long-distance supplier of Meals on Wheels?

parts.words: Long-distance supplier of Meals on Wheels?
parts.note: Meals on Wheels is a British charity delivering food to the housebound; here the wheels are those of a train serving meals on long journeys

explanation.surface: A charity van delivering food over long distances.
explanation.walkthrough: Meals on Wheels is a British service bringing hot meals to elderly people at home; the clue reads it as a train carriage serving food.
explanation.definitionFit: A dining carriage on a train serves meals to passengers on long rail journeys.

clue.text: Decline to accept one shilling for fund

indicators.note: to accept means the first word takes the others into itself

parts.note: to subside is to sink or decline
I is the Roman numeral one
S is the abbreviation for a shilling, an old British coin

explanation.surface: Refusing to take a single shilling for a fund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline to accept' looks like refusal, but SUBSIDE takes I and S inside. A shilling was a pre-1971 British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To subsidise something is to fund it, paying part of its cost.

clue.text: Unseemly male exploit's beginning behind the scenes

parts.note: off can mean improper or not acceptable, as in a bit off
a stag is a male deer

indicators.note: beginning takes the first letter of the word exploit's

explanation.surface: A man's shady exploit starts out of public view.
explanation.definitionFit: Offstage describes action out of the audience's sight, which is behind the scenes.

clue.text: Very much affected, as are one's neighbours

definitions.meaning: the people next door are literally at one's side

explanation.surface: Deeply moved, like the people living next door.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone overcome with emotion, while literally people next to one are by one's side.

clue.text: Artist's father a good person, I admitted

parts.note: dad means father

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so I goes inside the other letters

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a good person

explanation.surface: A painter's father is a fine person, I'll grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' looks like confessed but puts I inside A ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dadaist belonged to the Dada movement, an avant-garde art school, so is an artist.

clue.text: A great talker, Irish sailor recalled boring old times

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the reversed letters go inside

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, times

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A chatty Irish seaman reminisces tediously about the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like tedious, but means drilling: RATRI, made by 'recalled', goes into the old times.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratrix is an old word for a female orator, someone who speaks at length in public.

clue.text: Squanders benefit on drink

parts.note: use means benefit, as in of use
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone wastes their welfare money on alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'benefit' suggests state welfare, but means use.
explanation.definitionFit: To use up something is to exhaust it entirely, which is close to squandering it.

clue.text: Able seaman's leader knocked off

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter, here of seaman's

parts.note: knocked off is slang for killed

explanation.surface: A naval officer is murdered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Able seaman' reads as a rank, but 'Able' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Able and skilled both mean competent, having the ability to do something well.

clue.text: A painful affliction regularly hits rodents

parts.note: gout is a painful inflammation of the joints

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word hits

explanation.surface: A painful complaint strikes rodents often.
explanation.definitionFit: Agoutis are burrowing South American mammals related to guinea pigs, so they are rodents.

clue.text: Coverage of seed trial, part one?

parts.note: a test is a trial
A labels the first part, as in part A

explanation.surface: A seed test, first stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The testa is the botanical term for the hard outer coat of a seed.

clue.text: More artful hosts aren't commonly of better character

indicators.note: hosts means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: slier means craftier, more artful
ain't is the colloquial form of aren't

explanation.surface: Sly people entertain those who aren't, it's commonly said, more virtuous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosts' looks like a noun but is the container verb; 'commonly' marks the dialect contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Saintlier means more saintly, more virtuous in character.

clue.text: Believer cheers after god succeeded

indicators.note: after places the cheers piece behind the others

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees
ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A worshipper cheers once a deity has triumphed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rastafarian is a follower of the Rastafari religion, so a believer.

clue.text: Writer's moggy perhaps given nothing to eat

indicators.note: to eat means the outer word takes the other inside

parts.note: a moggy, British slang for a cat, is an example of a pet
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A writer's cat is given no food.
explanation.walkthrough: A moggy is British slang for an ordinary cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A poet is someone who writes verse, so a writer.

clue.text: Playing extra beat, a consequence of overassessment?

indicators.note: playing about with something rearranges it, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A musician adds an extra beat.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface hides the tax sense of assessment.
explanation.definitionFit: If a tax bill is overassessed, the overpayment comes back as a refund from the revenue.
